newsitem.title: UK: CBI sees risk of protectionism if EMU flops.
newsitem.headline: CBI sees risk of protectionism if EMU flops.

text.p: Any failure of European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) to get off the ground, or collapse shortly after it begins, could start a period of protectionist behaviour in Europe, an industry conference heard on Wednesday.
"In the UK, we shouldn't be sanguine about the potential for EMU failure if we are on the sidelines," said Peter Agar, deputy general of the Confederation of British Industry.
"If EMU fails, the single market would crumble and protectionist barriers will spring up. Europe will enter a long period of stagnation."
Even if EMU survives, John Stevens, Member of European Parliament, said there may be a temptation for Europe to lose the competitive edge.
He said the increased likelihood of a broad-based euro, with perhaps only Greece and Sweden outside, would force Britain's Labour government to agree to joining.
"Otherwise, a weak euro could mean that sterling is significantly overvalued," said Stevens.
He said it was important for EMU to be capable of meeting competitive challenges from outside the union.
"The ghost at the feast is protectionism," he said.
